verdict: Chapter 6 cites only [2], [4], [13], [18], [20], [24] and [33], and every citation is appropriate for its sentence (DID/VC survey for the identity principle, threshold committees correctly described as a precedent applied to consent approval rather than credential issuance, dynamic-consent works for lifecycle change, and blockchain integrity works for auditability), so citation relevance is not a concern. The main readiness problems are internal consistency: the RO3 outcome is written as ALLOW in Eq. (55), in the explicit threshold condition and in the RO6 threshold property although Algorithm 3 returns ACTIVATED, the RO4 closing rule omits the temporal and jurisdictional conjuncts that Eq. (59) and Algorithm 4 enforce, Eq. (70) is still called 'the CA3 extension' although the chapter states it is implemented, Eq. (18) is misdescribed as temporal, and Algorithms 1 and 3 use variables (L validation, g, siga, addrp, addrr) that their Require lines do not introduce. Cross-references to Figures 10–16, to Section 6.8.5, to the 23 tests and to block 11,771,307 all resolve correctly, so after the listed fixes (about a dozen small textual corrections plus one explanatory sentence on the Groth16 proof) the chapter is ready for submission.
